overview: This Senate resolution supports naming October 2026 "Substance Use & Misuse Prevention Month" to raise awareness of drug and alcohol misuse. It notes estimates that in 2025 tens of millions of Americans aged 12 and older engaged in binge drinking, used illegal drugs or had a substance use disorder, and that starting substance use as a teenager is linked to problems later in life. The resolution states the Senate's support for effective prevention programs and for efforts to address drug addiction and overdoses. It does not create programs or spend money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say drawing attention to prevention, especially among young people, encourages families, schools and communities to act before substance use becomes addiction.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it does not change any law or provide new funding for prevention or treatment programs.
